lead_headline: Weekend restaurant sweep nets 7 new leads—C Burger, China BBQ, Dunkin' openings offset 303 Ramen fire closure—as foreclosure filings slide 33% to 33 cases.

restaurant.blurb: 7 new leads since Friday push the active tracker to 28 total (14 openings, 14 closures). Weekend openings: China BBQ launched in Chaffee Park, The Barn South Broadway debuted in Rosedale, Dunkin' popped up in Regis at the old Church's Chicken site. C Burger (regenerative beef smashburgers) hit McGregor Square Saturday. Closures: Sawa Mediterranean pivoted to catering-only near DU. 303 Ramen remains sidelined post-fire, Colfax and Cream shuttered both Capitol Hill and Wash Park West locations after rapid 2025 expansion imploded.

foreclosure.blurb: 33 new filings this week—down 33% from last week's 49, extending the retreat from February's spike. Total exposure: $11.1M, with top case at $628K (Douglas County's 5118 Lumos Lane). 43 auctions teed up for next seven days. Weld County anchors the docket at 315 active cases, Arapahoe trails at 290. Three-week deceleration confirms filing pace normalizing after winter surge—market cooling or just a breather before spring remains the question.

reputation.blurb: 2 mentions today cap a 45-citation week across 14 unique sources—all of it representing the tracker's entire lifespan since launch. Denver Post dominates with 18 pickups, Facebook grabs 6, Hoodline adds 5. Monday highlights: Post's Denver coverage index page, Facebook share of Live Nation/Ticketmaster antitrust allegations. Google News RSS captured 44 of 45 total discoveries. Week's breakout: tracker went from zero to operational, establishing baseline but lacking historical comparison for trend analysis.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +3 since Friday (4 new, 1 canceled) lifts March to +3 MTD (+0.4/day), with 90-day cumulative at +71. Weekend steadied the ship after last week's Thursday −4 wobble. Past two weeks paint volatility: Feb 24's catastrophic −9 preceded a robust +12 five-day run, but early March stumbled with back-to-back negatives before Friday-Sunday's +3 recovery. YTD pace of +1.1/day still outperforms March's tepid 0.4 rate—question is whether weekend momentum signals stabilization or just noise.
